scalars.scalar_value: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.

items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
6 - 10 years of related experience.
Minimum of 6 years of experience with data design and information architecture, including data modeling.
Initiates, designs and deploys large scale systems. Designs highly complex user systems interfaces, business software prototypes and new systems or major enhancements to existing programs. (45% time)

Translates high-level business requirements from stakeholders and data stewards into granular technical data specifications. Analyzes the feasibility of integrating new data streams into the existing ecosystem and evaluates how changes in transactional source systems will impact downstream analytical models and institutional metrics. (20% time)

Applies advanced IT architecture concepts to function as the highest level technical expert. Often serves as consultant to management. May lead or provide guidance to large development team in design of highly complex software systems. Advises on selection of technological purchases with regards to processing, data storage, data access and software development. (15% time)

Defines the source of truth for institutional datasets (e.g., Student, Faculty, Course). Establishes the structural standards that ensure data is secure by design. Ensures that the Semantic Layer is architected so that disparate departments can consume data through a unified, governed lens. Together with data stewards, ensure the data dictionary is complete and up-to-date for all institutional datasets. (15% time)

Partners with Data Engineering, Infrastructure, and Database Administration teams to ensure that architectural designs are successfully deployed and performant. Acts as the bridge between the "Blueprint" (Design) and the "Build" (Implementation), ensuring the final technical environment accurately reflects the intended data models and security protocols. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Constantly
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Sit: Constantly
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally
Knowledge of software, database, infrastructure or other IT function. Knowledge relating to the design and development of software across the organization.

May require skills in web software, web software language and object oriented software concepts. May require knowledge of network protocols and how they are used on a large (campus/medical center/OP-wide, institution-wide or beyond) network. May require advanced knowledge of data storage, processing analysis and visualization technologies and how they are used in administrative and/or academic endeavors at a large, top-tier research university or medical center.
Knowledge of other related areas of IT. Ability to apply department processes and procedures to work.

Advanced ability to translate vague business requests from University stakeholders into granular technical specifications and data requirements. Familiarity with common University data domains (e.g., Student Information Systems (SIS), Financials, CRM, and Research Administration).

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization.
Expert-level SQL skills to query complex datasets, validate models, and perform deep-dive data profiling across disparate systems.
Ability to understand business needs and how business systems can support those needs.

Ability to serve as a "Lead by Example" figure, providing clear, actionable blueprints and documentation that reduce friction for implementation teams rather than creating bureaucratic hurdles. Advanced interpersonal skills with the ability to navigate complex institutional silos. Must be able to "sell" the long-term value of structured architecture to stakeholders who may be focused on short-term delivery speed.
Demonstrated ability to work with others from diverse backgrounds.
Experience with automated data cataloging or lineage tools (e.g., Collibra, Alation, or open-source equivalents).
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team. Demonstrates problem solving skills. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines.
Knowledge of the use of AI agents in day-to-day work and how to support other teams through agents to guide their architecture work.
Demonstrated ability to translate business needs into long-term architecture solutions. Expertise relating to the design and development of software across the organization.
Advanced knowledge of data storage, processing, and analysis and how they are used in administrative, medical and/or academic endeavors.

Understanding of and experience with key modeling and description languages used to map complex business processes to architectural components, develop common data resource architectures, and create reference frameworks.
Experience with the integration of complex, diverse, internally and externally developed implementations of business functions to build scalable systems.
Mastery of both Relational Modeling (3rd Normal Form) for transactional systems and Dimensional Modeling (Star/Snowflake schemas) and denormalized for data warehousing.

Ability to create high-level Entity Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) and data flow diagrams that serve as the authoritative blueprint for development teams. Ability to explain complex architectural concepts to both "downstream" Data Engineers and "upstream" Software Developers.
Knowledge of Master Data Management (MDM) and the ability to define and maintain a centralized data dictionary/business glossary.
Proven ability to establish, document, and evangelize enterprise data standards that cross-functional teams (Software Dev and Data Engineering) are motivated to follow.
